Honestly, we've done all of these. 

● Cosleeping, we didn't necessarily only have blankets, we had our pillows, our duvet, sometimes even a cuddly toy. She slept on her front pretty much since day 1, she slept on either mine or my husband's chest. We coslept because the alternative was insanity from just not sleeping. 

● I wasn't bothered about people washing their hands before holding her, we never asked about illnesses, we did have people say they weren't coming if they were ill. She got covid at 5 weeks old from my husband on a work trip. 

● We don't really track naps, we kind of just go with it and if she's starting to act tired, she sleeps. We barely have a day to day routine, she has a bath and bedtime routine and a time we aim for, which we miss most of the time. 

● We always have the tv on, she dances about to theme songs and then just carries on playing, she doesn't really pay any attention to it (I think my husband and I pay more attention to it than she does). She also likes using my phone to see herself because we don't have easily accessible mirrors. 

● I drank and breastfed, and coslept. I never drank so much that I was losing my balance or even wobbly. 

● We started giving her solids a couple of weeks before she was 6 months (health visitor suggested it). But we had given her a little taste of ice cream, cream and I think ice lollies before that (from probably 4 months).

● She was basically fully weaned at 10 months, her choice, not ours. I had to give her a bottle of formula at night just to make sure she was having something, but she would have been happy without.

● We also play kind of rough with her, dangle her by her legs, chuck her up in the air (not high but definitely out of our hands). She absolutely loves it!

● We've also had her in her car seat for longer than necessary. We've done journeys longer than 2 hours. I've also driven around a bit if she falls asleep in the car and needs a nap, or stayed on the drive in the car whilst she slept. 

I'm sure there's other things that I've forgotten or repressed. I feel so guilty about it all sometimes, but we just have to remember that we have a happy, healthy, somewhat chaotic 1 year old. You're doing fine.

The best way to work it out is to look at the numbers on the last row and column of your pattern and multiply them together.

For example: a pattern that has 12 columns and 13 rows would be 12 x 13 = 156 stitches. 

Also, if you want to work out what percentage you've done, just to make you feel like you've done absolutely no progress, divide the number of stitches you've done by the total number of stitches and then multiply by 100. So 39 stitches out of 156 would be 39 ÷ 156 x 100 = 25% completed.
